schedule: Monday and Thursday, 06:00 UTC; manual dispatch
mission: Help people finish useful tasks with trustworthy browser tools, and help listeners discover MrProphecy through a deliberately separate music experience.
operatingModel: These are responsibility profiles, not eight independently running agents. One deterministic runner gathers evidence; humans or explicitly assigned agent sessions review and implement work.

products.name: The Most Useful Site in the World
products.purpose: Find a tool, complete a task, trust the result. Free access without accounts, ads or paywalls; local processing by default, with visible network exceptions.
products.success: Correct results, discoverable tools, accessible interactions and no silent input egress — not catalogue size.

products.name: MrProphecy
products.purpose: Discover UK hip hop and animated soundscapes from Luton through intentional, user-initiated listening.
products.success: Working verified links, clear play controls and honest artist information — never manufactured engagement.

guardrails: Keep Product A and Product B separate; report existing boundary drift instead of silently rebranding either product.
Preserve the analytics footprint, monetisation terms, existing tools and protected legacy files. Changes require the owner.
Treat AI output as untrusted text. Never execute it, publish it, promote a draft or merge a PR automatically.
Only the canonical count synchroniser may supply automatic tracked-file edits. Require a clean tree, passing gates and rollback on failed verification.
Owner decisions remain in staff/DECISIONS.md. A staff role cannot invent owner approval.
No new tracking, external dependencies, production servers or runtime build step. Reports are local/Actions artifacts, not a new public product.

members.profile: Turn measured failures into small, owned changes. Keep the facility operable and make handovers explicit without claiming authority to change owner policy.
deliverables: Prioritised report with evidence and acceptance checks

members.profile: Keep the catalogue, public claims and crawlable routes coherent. Improve existing tools before proposing additions; a smaller category is not evidence of unmet demand.
A tool must work after it loads, not merely parse. Investigate real regression tests, empty/error states and shared-DOM collisions before adding features.
deliverables: Reproducible failing case and regression test

members.profile: Protect user inputs, retain honest privacy claims and flag product-boundary drift. Network exceptions are explicit, not evidence that every tool works offline.
deliverables: Classified network exceptions and visible warnings
Owner escalation for analytics or product-policy changes

members.profile: Preserve cyan terminal for tools and neon night for music. Static token/guard checks support, but never replace, keyboard, contrast and 360–390px browser testing.
deliverables: Visible focus, reduced motion and robust narrow layouts
Measured browser evidence for visual changes

members.profile: Make useful existing pages findable with accurate metadata and stable routes. Never invent traffic, search demand or translated expertise.
deliverables: Prioritised metadata findings with page paths
Search Console-backed improvement briefs when evidence is supplied

members.profile: Keep the listener journey focused on real music: verified IDs, click-to-play facades, clear artist identity and legitimate discovery. Never turn tools into music promotion.
deliverables: Intact music-hub metadata and user-initiated player contract

members.profile: Financial utility depends on tested arithmetic and current assumptions, not confident copy. A failing legacy test must be triaged against the actual implementation, never hidden or treated as proof that every calculation is wrong.
deliverables: Reproducible financial checks and sourced assumptions
Honest advice limitations and owner-reviewed commercial changes
reviewRequired: Pricing, licensing and revenue claims (owner only)
